mainTopic: How many לחיים or פסין are needed to permit carrying in a מבוי or a breached חצר, and how big they must be.
overview: This amud deals with the markers needed to permit carrying on שבת in a מבוי (alleyway) and in a חצר (courtyard) whose wall has been broken open. It opens with a story: רבי אליעזר tells his student to add a second לחי, and the student asks, 'Do I need to close it up?' The גמרא tries to prove from this that רבי אליעזר also requires a קורה, but rejects the proof. רב אשי explains רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's statement: a narrow alley needs only a לחי or a קורה. Then רב אחלי (some say רב יחיאל) says that an alley up to four טפחים wide needs nothing at all. The גמרא then discusses פסי חצר, the strips of wall left beside a breach: רבי requires two, while the רבנן allow one. Contradictions in the statements of רבי יוחנן and of שמואל are resolved the same way: a פס on one side must be four טפחים, but פסין on both sides can each be any size. Along the way we learn that the חכמים were lenient with partitions over water. The amud ends with a ברייתא about a sea inlet entering a courtyard and a question about how carrying inside that courtyard can be permitted. The answer to that question continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר tells his student to add a second side post
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues the story. רבי אליעזר finds his student living in a מבוי with only one לחי and tells him to add another. The student protests that this would close the alley off, and רבי אליעזר answers: let it be closed, so what?
steps.simpleTranslation: (רבי אליעזר went to his student רבי יוסי בן פרידה) in אובלין. He found him living in an alleyway that had only one side post. He said to him: 'My son, put up another side post.' The student said: 'Do I need to close it up?' רבי אליעזר said: 'Let it be closed. What does it matter?'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is quoting a story from a ברייתא that it will soon use as evidence about רבי אליעזר's view. The beginning of the story (that רבי אליעזר went to visit his student רבי יוסי בן פרידה) was earlier.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר holds that a מבוי needs two לחיים, so one side post is not enough for him. The student's reaction, 'Do I need to close it up?', is the key line. The גמרא will soon analyze exactly what 'closing it up' could mean.

keyTerms.meaning: An alleyway that opens onto a public area; it needs a small marker to allow carrying inside on שבת.
A side post placed at the alley's entrance.
To close it up / seal it.
So what? What does it matter?

steps.confusionAlert: This amud begins in the middle of a sentence. 'לאובלין' means 'to אובלין,' the town where the student lived. The person who went there is רבי אליעזר.

phrases.english: to Ovelin, and he found him
phrases.notes: This continues the story: רבי אליעזר went to his student רבי יוסי בן פרידה.

phrases.english: living in an alleyway
that had only one side post.
He (Rabbi Eliezer) said to him: My son,
put up another side post.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ: וְכִי לְסוֹתְמוֹ אֲנִי צָרִיךְ?
phrases.english: He (the student) said to him: Do I need to close it up?
phrases.notes: This is the key phrase the גמרא will analyze.

phrases.english: He said to him: Let it be closed; what does it matter?

steps.triggerLanguage: לְאוֹבָלִין וּמְצָאוֹ שֶׁיּוֹשֵׁב בְּמָבוֹי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא that was introduced on the previous amud as evidence for what רבי אליעזר requires.
steps.raayaObject: Whether רבי אליעזר requires a קורה in addition to two לחיים.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story of רבי אליעזר and רבי יוסי בן פרידה in אובלין.

steps.title: Where בית שמאי and בית הלל actually disagree
steps.stepSummary: Within the same תוספתא, רבן שמעון בן גמליאל explains the scope of the dispute. An alley narrower than four אמות needs nothing. For an alley from four to ten אמות wide, בית שמאי require both a לחי and a קורה, while בית הלל require only one of them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל said: בית שמאי and בית הלל did not argue about an alleyway less than four cubits wide, which needs nothing. What did they argue about? About one wider than four cubits and up to ten. בית שמאי say: a side post and a cross beam. בית הלל say: either a side post or a cross beam.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with רבן שמעון בן גמליאל describing exactly where בית שמאי and בית הלל disagree about fixing up a מבוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This sets the basic range of opinions. Under four אמות, nothing is needed. From four to ten אמות, בית שמאי require a לחי and a קורה, while בית הלל accept either one. Against this background, רבי אליעזר's demand for two לחיים stands out as especially strict.

keyTerms.meaning: A cross beam placed across the top of the alley's entrance.
Either a side post or a cross beam.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two houses. בית שמאי, the stricter view, require both a לחי and a קורה. בית הלל are satisfied with either one.

phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel said:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא נֶחְלְקוּ בֵּית שַׁמַּאי וּבֵית הִלֵּל
phrases.english: Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel did not disagree

phrases.aramaic: עַל מָבוֹי שֶׁהוּא פָּחוֹת מֵאַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת
phrases.english: about an alleyway that is less than four cubits wide
that it needs nothing at all;
about what did they disagree?

phrases.aramaic: עַל רָחָב מֵאַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת וְעַד עֶשֶׂר.
phrases.english: about one wider than four cubits and up to ten.
For Beit Shammai say: a side post and a cross beam,

phrases.aramaic: וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים: אוֹ לֶחִי אוֹ קוֹרָה.
phrases.english: and Beit Hillel say: either a side post or a cross beam.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל: לֹא נֶחְלְקוּ בֵּית שַׁמַּאי וּבֵית הִלֵּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same תוספתא, giving the broader dispute in which the story sits.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Under four אמות, nothing is needed. From four to ten אמות, בית שמאי require a לחי and a קורה, and בית הלל require either a לחי or a קורה.

steps.title: The proof from the word 'close it up'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא focuses on the student's words, 'Do I need to close it up?' If רבי אליעזר requires two לחיים plus a קורה, the entrance is framed on both sides and on top, and the student's complaint makes sense. If he requires only two לחיים, the top stays open, so what would 'closing it up' mean?
steps.simpleTranslation: In any case, the ברייתא teaches: 'Do I need to close it up?' It makes sense if you say he requires two side posts and a cross beam; that is why the student said, 'Do I need to close it up?' But if you say he requires side posts without a cross beam, what does 'to close it up' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא uses the story as a proof. It argues that the student's words show רבי אליעזר requires a קורה in addition to two לחיים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With two side posts and a beam on top, the entrance is framed on three sides and looks closed off. With two side posts alone, the top is still open, so the word 'close' seems out of place. That suggests רבי אליעזר requires a קורה as well.

keyTerms.meaning: In any case, it teaches (a formula that points to the key detail in a source).
It makes sense if you say...

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the main attempt in the sugya to settle what רבי אליעזר requires. The whole proof rests on reading one word, לסותמו, precisely.

phrases.english: In any case, it teaches:
'Do I need to close it up?'
It makes sense if you say he requires two side posts and a cross beam —
that is why he said:
'Do I need to close it up?'

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִי אָמְרַתְּ לְחָיַיִן בְּלֹא קוֹרָה —
phrases.english: But if you say he requires side posts without a cross beam —
what does 'to close it up' mean?
phrases.notes: The top of the entrance would still be open.

steps.triggerLanguage: קָתָנֵי מִיהַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the story cited in step 1 and draws an inference from its wording.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי אליעזר requires two לחיים and a קורה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The student's words 'וכי לסותמו אני צריך' in the תוספתא.

steps.title: The student may have meant closing with side posts
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. The student may have meant: 'Do I need to close up the sides with side posts?' Two לחיים close in both sides of the entrance even without a קורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what he was saying: 'Do I need to close it up with side posts?'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the proof from step 3. It offers a different reading of the student's words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Closing it up' can refer to the sides alone: with a לחי on each side, the entrance looks narrowed or closed in. So the story fits even if רבי אליעזר requires only two לחיים without a קורה. This proof therefore does not settle his view.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what he meant (a formula that reinterprets a statement).

steps.whatToRemember: The story does not prove that רבי אליעזר requires a קורה. 'Closing it up' could just mean adding side posts on both sides.

phrases.english: This is what he was saying:
Do I need to close it up with side posts?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי קָאָמַר: וְכִי לְסוֹתְמוֹ בִּלְחָיַיִן אֲנִי צָרִיךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of step 3 by reinterpreting the key word.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only this proof; it does not decide what רבי אליעזר actually holds.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed 'closing' must mean closing on top with a קורה. It can also mean closing the sides with לחיים.

steps.title: The משנה says a narrow alley still needs a post or beam
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's line that an alley narrower than four אמות needs nothing. It then challenges it from the משנה, which says such an alley is permitted with a לחי or a קורה. That implies it still needs something.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל said that בית שמאי and בית הלל do not argue about an alley narrower than four אמות, since it needs nothing. But we learned in the משנה: a student said before רבי עקיבא in the name of רבי ישמעאל that בית שמאי and בית הלל do not argue about an alley narrower than four אמות, since it is permitted with either a לחי or a קורה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes again a line from the תוספתא we just saw. This time it quotes it in order to attack it with a contradiction from our משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says a narrow alley needs 'nothing at all.' The משנה describes the same narrow alley and says it becomes permitted 'with a לחי or a קורה.' That means it does need at least one fix, so the two sources seem to clash.

keyTerms.meaning: 'But didn't we learn (in a משנה)?' This opens a challenge from a משנה.

steps.confusionAlert: Both sources talk about the SAME size, an alley narrower than four אמות. The clash is only about what that alley needs: 'nothing' versus 'a לחי or a קורה.'

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר מָר: אָמַר רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל:
phrases.english: The Master said: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel said:
phrases.notes: This quotes the תוספתא from Step 2 again.

phrases.aramaic: לֹא נֶחְלְקוּ בֵּית שַׁמַּאי וּבֵית הִלֵּל
phrases.english: Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel did not disagree
about an alley that is less than four cubits wide
that it does not need anything.
phrases.notes: This is the claim being challenged.

phrases.english: But didn't we learn in the Mishnah:

phrases.aramaic: מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל אָמַר תַּלְמִיד אֶחָד לִפְנֵי רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא:
phrases.english: In the name of Rabbi Yishmael, a certain student said before Rabbi Akiva:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא נֶחְלְקוּ בֵּית שַׁמַּאי וּבֵית הִלֵּל
phrases.english: Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel did not disagree

phrases.aramaic: עַל מָבוֹי שֶׁהוּא פָּחוֹת מֵאַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת
phrases.english: about an alley that is less than four cubits wide

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁהוּא נִיתָּר אוֹ בְּלֶחִי אוֹ בְּקוֹרָה!
phrases.english: that it is permitted with either a side post or a crossbeam!
phrases.notes: So it does need something.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא אֲנַן תְּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the student-story discussion and goes back to analyze the רבן שמעון בן גמליאל line from Step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's claim that an alley under four אמות needs nothing
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה says the same narrow alley is permitted with a לחי or a קורה, so it does need something. That contradicts 'nothing.'

steps.title: 'Nothing' means nothing beyond one post or beam
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי explains that 'needs nothing' means it needs no extra requirements. It does not need a לחי and a קורה as בית שמאי require, and it does not need two לחיים as רבי אליעזר requires. It needs only a לחי or a קורה, as בית הלל require.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: this is what he means. It does not need a לחי and a קורה like בית שמאי, and it does not need two לחיים like רבי אליעזר. Rather, it needs a לחי or a קורה, like בית הלל.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי resolves the contradiction by reinterpreting the word 'nothing.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Nothing' is relative. It means nothing more than the minimum. Even בית שמאי and רבי אליעזר agree that a narrow alley needs only one לחי or one קורה, which matches בית הלל and fits the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: 'This is what he means.' This reinterprets a statement.

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows there are three positions for a wide alley: בית שמאי (a לחי and a קורה), רבי אליעזר (two לחיים), and בית הלל (one of them). In a narrow alley, all three agree on בית הלל's minimum.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said: This is what he means:

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ צָרִיךְ לֶחִי וְקוֹרָה כְּבֵית שַׁמַּאי,
phrases.english: It does not need a side post and a crossbeam, like Beit Shammai,
nor two side posts, like Rabbi Eliezer,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא: אוֹ לֶחִי אוֹ קוֹרָה, כְּבֵית הִלֵּל.
phrases.english: rather: either a side post or a crossbeam, like Beit Hillel.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי, הָכִי קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in Step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of wording ('nothing' means nothing extra)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Needs nothing' means no לחי or קורה at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Needs nothing' means nothing beyond בית הלל's single לחי or קורה.

steps.title: How narrow before an alley needs nothing at all?
steps.stepSummary: Since even a narrow alley needs a לחי or a קורה, the גמרא asks at what width an alley truly needs nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how much?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short follow-up question and sets up the next step's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 6 showed that 'under four אמות' still needs one fix. So there must be a smaller width where no fix is needed at all, and the גמרא wants that number.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And how much?' A request for a measurement.

phrases.english: And how much?
phrases.notes: How narrow must the alley be to need nothing at all?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכַמָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows up on Step 6: if under four אמות still needs something, what width needs nothing?
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The maximum width of an alley that needs no לחי or קורה at all

steps.title: Up to four handbreadths needs nothing
steps.stepSummary: רב אחלי, or some say רב יחיאל, answers that an alley up to four טפחים wide needs nothing at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחלי said, and some say it was רב יחיאל: up to four (טפחים).
steps.whatsHappening: The answer: an alley up to four טפחים wide needs no לחי or קורה at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'four' here is four טפחים (handbreadths), not four אמות. An opening that small is not treated as a real opening, so it needs no fix.

keyTerms.meaning: Handbreadths, a much smaller unit than אַמּוֹת (implied here)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't confuse this 'four' with the 'four אמות' from before. Here it means four טפחים, which is much narrower.
steps.whatToRemember: Under four טפחים: nothing needed. Under four אמות: a לחי or a קורה (all agree). Four to ten אמות: the dispute among בית שמאי, בית הלל, and רבי אליעזר.

phrases.english: Rav Achlei said:
and some say it was Rav Yechiel:
Up to four (handbreadths).
phrases.notes: Four טפחים, not four אמות.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַחְלַי וְאִיתֵּימָא רַב יְחִיאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Up to four טפחים, an alley needs nothing at all.

steps.title: The Sages agree with רבי אליעזר about courtyard posts
steps.stepSummary: רב, quoted through a chain, says that the חכמים agree with רבי אליעזר about the posts of a breached courtyard (פסי חצר). Two posts are needed, one on each side of the breach.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said in the name of רב ירמיה בר אבא in the name of רב: the חכמים agree with רבי אליעזר regarding the posts of a courtyard.
steps.whatsHappening: A new statement. רב limits the argument with רבי אליעזר: in a courtyard, everyone agrees with him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר required two לחיים for an alley, and the חכמים disagreed. רב says that if a courtyard's wall is broken open, even the חכמים require wall pieces (פסים) on both sides, just as רבי אליעזר does.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The חכמים agree.' The other side concedes on this point.
The upright wall strips left on the sides of a breached courtyard wall

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת אָמַר רַב יִרְמְיָה בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said that Rav Yirmeya bar Abba said that Rav said:
The Sages concede to Rabbi Eliezer
regarding the upright boards of a courtyard.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת אָמַר רַב יִרְמְיָה בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from alley widths to applying רבי אליעזר's two-post view to a courtyard.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In a breached courtyard, even the חכמים require פסים on both sides, like רבי אליעזר.

steps.title: רב נחמן: the halacha follows רבי אליעזר for courtyard posts
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן gives a different wording. He says the הלכה follows רבי אליעזר about courtyard posts.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב נחמן said: the הלכה follows רבי אליעזר regarding the posts of a courtyard.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן gives his own version of the courtyard rule, worded differently from רב's.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב said 'the חכמים agree,' which means there is no dispute about courtyards. רב נחמן says 'the הלכה follows רבי אליעזר,' which suggests there is a dispute and he is deciding it. In practice, both require two posts. The difference is whether the חכמים disagree with רבי אליעזר.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The הלכה follows...' This decides between disputing views.

steps.whyThisMatters: The different wording ('agree' versus 'the הלכה follows') signals two different ways of seeing the courtyard case.

phrases.english: And Rav Nachman said:
The halacha follows Rabbi Eliezer
regarding the upright boards of a courtyard.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב נַחְמָן אָמַר הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers an alternative wording to רב's statement in Step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה follows רבי אליעזר that a breached courtyard requires פסים on both sides.

steps.title: The agreeing חכמים are רבי
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק explains that the חכמים who 'agree' with רבי אליעזר in רב's statement are רבי (רבי יהודה הנשיא).
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: Who are the ones who agree? רבי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to רב's statement in Step 9, that 'the חכמים agree with רבי אליעזר.' It identifies exactly who those חכמים are: רבי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב's word 'מודים' (they agree) was vague, and it was unclear who agrees. רב נחמן בר יצחק says it refers to רבי, who also requires two פסין for a breached חצר, just as רבי אליעזר requires two לחיים.

keyTerms.meaning: Upright boards (wall remnants) beside a breach in a courtyard wall

steps.confusionAlert: 'רבי' with no name after it always means רבי יהודה הנשיא. It is not a general title for 'some rabbi.'

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
Who are 'those who agree'? It is Rabbi (Yehuda HaNasi).
phrases.notes: Refers back to רב's statement in Step 9.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן מוֹדִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Clarifies who is meant by 'the חכמים agree' in רב's version (Step 9).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The 'agreeing חכמים' is רבי, who also requires two פסין for a breached חצר.

steps.title: The word הלכה implies a dispute with the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: Because רב נחמן said 'the הלכה follows רבי אליעזר,' there must be a dispute. The ones who disagree with רבי are the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he says 'the הלכה is,' that implies they disagree. Who disagrees with him? The רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now looks at רב נחמן's version from Step 10. It points out that saying 'the הלכה is' only makes sense if someone disagrees, and it names who that is: the רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You only need to rule 'the הלכה follows X' when there is a disagreement. So רב נחמן's wording shows there is an opinion against רבי, and that opinion belongs to the רבנן. The next step brings the source.

phrases.english: 'The halacha is' implies that they disagree;
[who disagrees with him?] The Rabbis.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲלָכָה מִכְּלָל דִּפְלִיגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from רב's version (מודים) to רב נחמן's version (הלכה) and draws an inference from its wording.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is a dispute: the רבנן disagree with רבי about פסי חצר.

steps.title: The ברייתא showing the dispute between the רבנן and רבי
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that according to the רבנן a breached חצר is permitted with one פס, while רבי requires two פסין.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught in a ברייתא: A courtyard becomes permitted with one board. רבי says: with two boards.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא as the source for the dispute it just described. It shows both opinions side by side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא confirms both identifications. רבי needs two פסין, matching רבי אליעזר's two לחיים, so he is the 'agreeing' one. The רבנן need only one, so they are the ones who disagree.

keyTerms.meaning: An upright board or piece of wall

steps.whatToRemember: For a breached חצר, the רבנן allow one פס. רבי (like רבי אליעזר) requires two, one on each side of the breach. רב נחמן rules like רבי.

phrases.english: As it was taught: A courtyard is permitted with one board.
Rabbi says: With two boards.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides the source text for the identifications made in Steps 11 and 12.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי requires two פסין and the רבנן disagree.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: חצר ניתרת בפס אחד; רבי אומר בשני פסין.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן requires two פסין
steps.stepSummary: רבי אסי quotes רבי יוחנן: a breached חצר needs two פסין.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אסי said in the name of רבי יוחנן: A courtyard needs two boards.
steps.whatsHappening: A new statement is brought. רבי יוחנן also holds like רבי that two פסין are needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This adds an אמורא from ארץ ישראל to the side of רבי. It will soon be challenged by another quote from רבי יוחנן.

keyTerms.meaning: Two boards, one on each side of the breach

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Asi said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan:
A courtyard requires two boards.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings another אמורא who holds like רבי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יוחנן, a breached חצר needs two פסין.

steps.title: רבי זירא challenges with another quote of רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא asks how רבי יוחנן could require two פסין, when רבי אסי himself quoted רבי יוחנן as saying פסי חצר must be four טפחים. That suggests one four-טפח board is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said to רבי אסי: Did רבי יוחנן really say that? But you yourself said in רבי יוחנן's name: The boards of a courtyard must be four טפחים!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא points out that רבי אסי's two quotes from רבי יוחנן seem to contradict each other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'four טפחים' rule sounds like it describes one board of four טפחים, which would mean a single פס works. That clashes with 'two פסין are needed.'

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי זֵירָא לְרַבִּי אַסִּי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said to Rabbi Asi:
Did Rabbi Yochanan really say this?
But aren't you the one who said
in the name of Rabbi Yochanan:
The boards of a courtyard must
have four (handbreadths) in them.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן הָכִי? וְהָא אַתְּ הוּא דְּאָמְרַתְּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the quote in Step 14 by citing a conflicting quote.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אסי's report that רבי יוחנן requires two פסין.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another report from רבי יוחנן says פסי חצר need four טפחים, which implies one four-טפח board is enough. So two boards would not be required.

steps.title: A suggested answer: four on each side
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests a possible answer: maybe רבי יוחנן means two boards, each four טפחים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say: four from here and four from there…
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא proposes an answer only to knock it down in the very next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The suggestion would combine both quotes: two פסין, each one four טפחים. Then there would be no contradiction. This idea is not accepted.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say (a suggested answer about to be rejected)

phrases.english: And if you say: four from this side
and four from that side —

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a possible way to reconcile the two quotes in Step 15.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two quotes clash: two boards versus one board of four.
steps.terutzMaskana: Perhaps two boards are needed, each four טפחים wide.

steps.title: The case of the 10-אמה and 11-אמה courtyards
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא permits a small courtyard 10 אמות wide that opens into a large one 11 אמות wide. That leaves only one אמה (6 טפחים) of wall, not 4+4=8, so 'four on each side' cannot be the rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't רב אדא בר אבימי teach before רבי חנינא (some say before רבי חנינא בר פפי): The small one is ten and the large one is eleven!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the suggestion from Step 16. It brings a ברייתא where the leftover wall is too small to have four טפחים on each side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The large courtyard is permitted even though only one extra אמה of wall remains, split between both sides. Six טפחים cannot make two boards of four טפחים each. So the rule cannot be 'four on each side.'
steps.confusionAlert: The numbers 10 and 11 are in אמות, not טפחים. The difference of one אמה equals six טפחים, which is less than the 8 that 'four on each side' would need.

phrases.english: But didn't Rav Adda bar Avimi teach
before Rabbi Chanina,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרִי לַהּ קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא בַּר פַּפִּי:
phrases.english: and some say before Rabbi Chanina bar Pappi:
The small one is ten (cubits),
and the large one is eleven!
phrases.notes: Only one cubit (6 handbreadths) of wall remains in total.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָתָנֵי רַב אַדָּא בַּר אֲבִימִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Knocks down the proposed answer of Step 16.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The suggestion that two boards of four טפחים each are required.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A ברייתא permits a case with only six טפחים of wall in total, so two four-טפח boards cannot be required.

steps.title: רבי זירא's resolution: one side needs four, two sides need any amount
steps.stepSummary: After returning from his sea travels, רבי זירא explained: a board on one side must be four טפחים, but boards on two sides can each be any tiny amount.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבי זירא came up from the sea, he explained it: On one side, four. On two sides, a little bit here and a little bit there.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא finally settles the contradiction between the two quotes of רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'four טפחים' rule covers the case of a board on only one side. The 'two פסין' rule covers boards on both sides, where each can be very small. This also fits the 10/11 אמה case, because any small amount on each side is enough.
steps.whatToRemember: פסי חצר: one board on one side must be four טפחים. Boards on both sides can each be any amount. Both statements of רבי יוחנן are true, each for a different setup.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the practical size rules for fixing a breached courtyard wall so that carrying is permitted on שבת.

phrases.aramaic: כִּי סָלֵיק רַבִּי זֵירָא מִיַּמֵּי פָּרְשַׁהּ:
phrases.english: When Rabbi Zeira came up from the sea, he explained it:
On one side, four (handbreadths);
from two sides —
any amount here and any amount there.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי סָלֵיק רַבִּי זֵירָא מִיַּמֵּי פָּרְשַׁהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in Step 15 in a way that fits the ברייתא of Step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing cases (one side versus two sides)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוחנן's two statements contradict, and 'four on each side' cannot work.
steps.terutzMaskana: Four טפחים applies to a single board on one side. Two boards on two sides need only any amount each.

steps.title: The Ten-and-Eleven Ruling Follows רבי and רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא of אדא בר אבימי, which requires an אמה difference between the courtyards, follows רבי, who requires two פסין, together with רבי יוסי, who requires each פס to be three טפחים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the ברייתא that אדא בר אבימי taught follows רבי, and he holds like רבי יוסי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the ברייתא from Step 17, which has the 10-אמה courtyard opening into the 11-אמה courtyard. It explains which opinions that ברייתא is built on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי זירא said two small boards of any size are enough, so why does the ברייתא need a full אמה of difference? The answer is that the ברייתא follows רבי, who requires two פסין, and רבי יוסי, who requires each one to be three טפחים. Three plus three is six טפחים, which is exactly one אמה.

keyTerms.meaning: And he holds like (adopts another Sage's view)

steps.confusionAlert: This does not cancel רבי זירא's rule. It only shows that this one ברייתא follows a stricter combination of opinions.

phrases.english: And that which Adda bar Avimi taught
phrases.notes: Refers to the ברייתא about the 10- and 11-אמה courtyards

phrases.english: is the view of Rabbi
phrases.notes: He requires two boards

phrases.english: and he holds like Rabbi Yosei.
phrases.notes: Each board must be three טפחים, so 3+3=6 טפחים, one אמה

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָדְתָנֵי אַדָּא בַּר אֲבִימִי רַבִּי הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רבי זירא's answer by explaining the ברייתא that seemed to contradict it
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attribution: assigning the ברייתא to a specific combination of תנאים
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא's one-אמה requirement seemed to be a universal rule
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא follows רבי and רבי יוסי, which gives 3+3 טפחים, one אמה

steps.title: שמואל: One Board Permits the Courtyard
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף, quoting רב יהודה in the name of שמואל, rules that a breached חצר is permitted with just one פס.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said in the name of רב יהודה, who said in the name of שמואל: A courtyard is permitted with one board.
steps.whatsHappening: A new statement opens a new discussion. According to שמואל, one strip of wall left at the breach is enough to keep the חצר permitted for carrying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is more lenient than the opinion of two פסין that רבי אסי quoted from רבי יוחנן. Here שמואל seems to require only a single פס.

keyTerms.meaning: One board, a single strip of wall

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said
Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
A courtyard is permitted with one board.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new line of discussion about how many פסין a breached חצר needs, this time according to שמואל
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A breached חצר is permitted with a single פס

steps.title: אביי: שמואל Told רב חנניה to Require Two Boards
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges this, because שמואל told רב חנניה בר שילא never to rule leniently unless most of the wall or two פסין remain.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to רב יוסף: Did שמואל really say this? But שמואל told רב חנניה בר שילא: Do not rule leniently in a real case unless most of the wall remains, or two boards remain!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks רב יוסף's quote. He cites a different statement of שמואל that seems to say the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In his instruction to רב חנניה בר שילא, שמואל required either רוב דופן or two פסין. That makes one פס not enough, so שמואל seems to contradict himself.

keyTerms.meaning: Did he really say this? (a formula that opens a challenge)
A practical case, an actual ruling
Two boards, one on each side of the breach

phrases.english: Abaye said to Rav Yosef:
Did Shmuel say this?
But didn't Shmuel say
to Rav Chananya bar Sheila:
You must not perform an action (issue a lenient ruling)
phrases.notes: Meaning: do not permit carrying in practice

phrases.english: except either with the majority of the wall
or with two boards!

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל הָכִי וְהָא אֲמַר לֵיהּ שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly challenges שמואל's ruling as quoted in Step 20
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's ruling that one פס is enough
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Contradiction: another instruction of שמואל requires רוב דופן or two פסין, so one פס should not be enough

steps.title: רב יוסף Cites the Shepherds' Village Case
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף cannot resolve the contradiction. Instead, he cites a real case where רב יהודה permitted a חצר with only one פס.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said to him: I don't know how to resolve it. But there was a real case in a shepherds' village, where an inlet of the sea entered a courtyard. It came before רב יהודה, and he required only one board.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף admits he has no answer to the contradiction. Instead, he brings practical evidence that רב יהודה, שמואל's student, actually ruled that one פס is enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He is supporting his tradition with a real ruling (מעשה) rather than by explaining the contradiction away. The case involved a לשון ים that broke into the חצר, and רב יהודה permitted it with a single פס.

keyTerms.meaning: A narrow inlet of the sea

phrases.english: He said to him: I do not know,
phrases.notes: He cannot resolve the contradiction

phrases.english: but there was an incident in a shepherds' village,
it was an inlet of the sea that entered a courtyard.
And it came before Rav Yehuda,
and he required only one board.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַאֲנָא לָא יָדַעְנָא דְּעוֹבָדָא הֲוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to אביי's challenge with a practical case instead of a resolution
steps.raayaObject: That one פס is enough to permit a breached חצר
steps.raayaSupportSource: A real ruling (מעשה) of רב יהודה in a shepherds' village

steps.title: אביי: Water Cases Are Special Leniencies
steps.stepSummary: אביי rejects the proof. A breach caused by a sea inlet involves water, and the חכמים were lenient with water, so no general rule can be learned from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: You are talking about an inlet of the sea? That is a leniency the חכמים allowed for water.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי knocks down רב יוסף's evidence. He shows that the case was special and does not apply to ordinary breached courtyards.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים accepted weaker מחיצות in cases involving water. So רב יהודה's one-פס ruling may apply only to water cases. Ordinary breaches would still need רוב דופן or two פסין, just as שמואל told רב חנניה בר שילא.

keyTerms.meaning: It is a leniency that the חכמים applied to water

steps.whatToRemember: רב יהודה's one-פס ruling in the sea-inlet case cannot serve as proof, because water cases get special leniency. The contradiction in שמואל's statements returns (Step 25) and is resolved in Step 26.
steps.whyThisMatters: This introduces the important principle that מחיצות involving water are treated more leniently. That principle appears in several places in הלכות שבת.

phrases.english: He said to him: You speak of an inlet of the sea?
That is a leniency that the Sages were lenient with regard to water.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְשׁוֹן יָם קָאָמְרַתְּ קַל הוּא שֶׁהֵקֵלּוּ חֲכָמִים בְּמַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in Step 22
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from the shepherds' village case, not the general topic
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The case involved water, where the חכמים were specially lenient, so it cannot set the rule for ordinary courtyards

steps.title: Proof that the Sages were lenient with water
steps.stepSummary: רבי טבלא asked רב whether a מחיצה תלויה permits carrying in a ruin. רב answered that it works only for water, because the חכמים were lenient with water.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי טבלא asked רב: Does a hanging partition permit carrying in a ruin? רב said to him: A hanging partition permits carrying only over water. This is a leniency that the חכמים made for water.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source that backs up אביי's claim that the חכמים made special leniencies for water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מחיצה תלויה is a wall that does not reach the ground. Normally it does not count as a wall. רב says it counts only over water, which proves that water cases get special leniency. This supports אביי's point that the sea-inlet case in Step 23 cannot teach us a general rule.

keyTerms.meaning: A hanging partition, a wall that does not reach the ground
It is a leniency the Sages made for water
He asked of him (a formal question to a teacher)

phrases.english: As Rabbi Tavla asked of Rav:
phrases.notes: The word 'כ' (as) shows this is brought as support for what came before.

phrases.english: A suspended partition: does it permit carrying in a ruin?
phrases.notes: The question is whether the remains of walls hanging in the air count as reaching down to the ground.

phrases.english: He said to him:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין מְחִיצָה תְּלוּיָה מַתֶּרֶת אֶלָּא בְּמַיִם,
phrases.english: A suspended partition permits only in the case of water;
it is a leniency that the Sages were lenient with water.
phrases.notes: This is the key line that supports אביי.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּדִבְעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי טַבְלָא מֵרַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports אביי's rejection in Step 23 by showing that the חכמים were generally lenient with water.
steps.raayaObject: אביי's claim that water cases get special leniency, so the sea-inlet case is no proof
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב's ruling to רבי טבלא that a מחיצה תלויה works only over water

steps.title: The contradiction in שמואל's rulings remains
steps.stepSummary: Even after all this, the contradiction between שמואל's two statements is still standing.
steps.simpleTranslation: In any case, it is difficult.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא admits that אביי's original question has not been answered. This line sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף's proof from the case of רב יהודה was rejected because it involved water. So we are back to the original problem from Step 21. שמואל permitted a חצר with one פס, yet he also told רב חנניה בר שילא to require most of the wall or two פסין.

keyTerms.meaning: It is difficult (a question still stands)

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new question. It brings back the same contradiction אביי raised in Step 21, which has not been answered yet. Step 26 answers it.

phrases.english: In any case, it is difficult.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִכׇּל מָקוֹם קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Since the proof in Step 22 was rejected in Step 23, the contradiction from Step 21 comes back.
steps.kashyaTarget: The contradiction between שמואל's ruling (one פס is enough) and his instruction to רב חנניה בר שילא (two פסין are needed)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The attempted support was rejected, so the two statements of שמואל still clash.

steps.title: One-sided board needs four handbreadths, two-sided boards any size
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא and רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע explain the contradiction. A single פס on one side must be four טפחים. If there are פסין on both sides, even tiny ones are enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב פפא and רב הונא, son of רב יהושע, came from their teacher's yeshiva, they explained it: From one side, the board must be four טפחים. From two sides, a tiny bit here and a tiny bit there is enough.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction by showing that the two statements of שמואל are talking about different situations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל's ruling that one פס is enough means one פס that is four טפחים wide. His instruction about two פסין means two פסין of any size, one on each side of the breach. So both statements are true, each in its own case.

keyTerms.meaning: From the house of their teacher, the yeshiva

steps.whyThisMatters: The answer shows that what matters is both the number of פסין and their size. One wide פס can work as well as two tiny ones.

phrases.aramaic: כִּי אֲתוֹ רַב פָּפָּא וְרַב הוּנָא
phrases.english: When Rav Pappa and Rav Huna came

phrases.aramaic: בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ מִבֵּי רַב פֵּירְשׁוּהָ:
phrases.english: son of Rav Yehoshua, from the house of their teacher, they explained it:
From one side: with four handbreadths;
phrases.notes: This matches שמואל's ruling that one פס is enough.

phrases.english: from two sides:
a bit here and a bit there.
phrases.notes: This matches שמואל's instruction about two פסין.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אֲתוֹ רַב פָּפָּא וְרַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ מִבֵּי רַב פֵּירְשׁוּהָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction that Step 25 said was still standing.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): each statement refers to a different setup
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It seemed that שמואל contradicted himself about whether one פס or two פסין are required.
steps.terutzMaskana: One פס works if it is four טפחים wide. Two פסין work even if each is tiny.

steps.title: רב פפא's difficulty with the explanation
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says that what still bothers him is שמואל's instruction to רב חנניה בר שילא to require most of the wall or two פסין. Given that a four-טפח פס is enough, the demand for most of the wall seems excessive.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: If something is difficult for me, this is what is difficult for me. שמואל said to רב חנניה בר שילא: Do not issue a ruling unless there is either most of the wall or two פסין.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא, who helped give the answer in Step 26, now points out a problem with it. This sets up the next step of the discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The explanation in Step 26 says a single פס of four טפחים is enough. If so, why did שמואל tell רב חנניה בר שילא to require רוב דופן (most of the wall), which can be much more than four טפחים? The next step spells this out.

keyTerms.term: אִי קַשְׁיָא לִי — הָא קַשְׁיָא לִי
keyTerms.meaning: If anything is difficult for me, this is what is difficult for me
A practical action, a real ruling
Most of the wall still standing

steps.confusionAlert: שמואל's instruction to רב חנניה בר שילא is the same one quoted in Step 21. It comes back here for a new purpose: to challenge the explanation in Step 26, not to repeat אביי's original question.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:

phrases.aramaic: אִי קַשְׁיָא לִי — הָא קַשְׁיָא לִי,
phrases.english: If it is difficult for me, this is difficult for me:

phrases.aramaic: דַּאֲמַר לֵיהּ שְׁמוּאֵל לְרַב חֲנַנְיָה בַּר שֵׁילָא:
phrases.english: That Shmuel said to Rav Ḥananya bar Sheila:
You must not perform a practical ruling

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אוֹ בְּרוֹב דּוֹפֶן אוֹ בִּשְׁנֵי פַסִּין.
phrases.english: unless with either most of the wall or two boards.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: אִי קַשְׁיָא לִי — הָא קַשְׁיָא לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the explanation given in Step 26.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's instruction to רב חנניה בר שילא requiring רוב דופן, read in light of the explanation that a four-טפח פס is enough
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a single four-טפח פס is enough, then שמואל's requirement of רוב דופן seems unnecessary. Why demand most of the wall when a four-טפח פס would do? (Step 28 spells this out.)

steps.title: Why require most of the wall when a four-handbreadth board is enough
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא spells out רב פפא's difficulty. If one פס of four טפחים works, why did שמואל tell רב חנניה בר שילא to build רוב דופן?
steps.simpleTranslation: Why do I need most of the wall? A board of four handbreadths should be enough!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now states exactly what was bothering רב פפא in Step 27. שמואל's instruction asked for more than his own rule seems to require.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 26 established that one פס on a single side works if it is four טפחים wide. So when שמואל told רב חנניה בר שילא to build רוב דופן (most of the wall), he seemed to demand too much. Building most of a long wall could be far more than four טפחים.

keyTerms.meaning: Most of the wall: building up more than half the width of the breached side
An upright board four טפחים wide

phrases.english: Why do I need most of the wall?
phrases.notes: Refers to שמואל's instruction to רב חנניה בר שילא.

phrases.english: A board of four should suffice!
phrases.notes: Based on the resolution in Step 26.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמָה לִי רוֹב דּוֹפֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the content of רב פפא's lingering difficulty from Step 27.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's instruction to רב חנניה בר שילא to build רוב דופן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שמואל's own rule says one four-טפח פס is enough, so requiring most of the wall seems unnecessary.

steps.title: A seven-handbreadth wall does not solve the problem either
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא considers saying שמואל meant a wall only seven טפחים wide, where four טפחים is most of it. It rejects this, because by רב אחלי's rule a little over three טפחים should then be enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say that 'most of the wall' means a wall seven handbreadths wide, where four is most of the wall, then why do I need four? Three and a bit should be enough! For רב אחלי, and some say רב יחיאל, said: up to four handbreadths needs nothing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests a way out and then knocks it down, which makes the question even stronger.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Suppose the breached side is seven טפחים wide. Building 'most' of it would then mean four טפחים, which matches the פס rule. But if you build just over three טפחים, the gap left over is less than four. רב אחלי says a gap of up to four טפחים needs no fix at all. So four טפחים would still be more than needed.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say: introduces a possible answer, often one that will be rejected
Three טפחים and a tiny bit more
Up to four: רב אחלי's rule that a gap under four טפחים needs nothing

steps.confusionAlert: The phrase 'וכי תימא' introduces an answer the גמרא is about to reject. It is not the גמרא's own conclusion.

phrases.english: And if you say: what does 'with most of the wall' mean?
It means with a wall of seven
phrases.notes: A breached side seven טפחים wide.

phrases.english: where four is most of the wall
Then why do I need four?
Three and a bit should suffice!
phrases.notes: The remaining gap would then be less than four.

phrases.english: For Rav Achlei said
and some say it was Rav Yechiel: up to four!
phrases.notes: A gap of up to four טפחים needs nothing.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא מַאי בְּרוֹב דּוֹפֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Blocks a possible defense of שמואל and so strengthens the question from Step 28.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that רוב דופן refers to a seven-טפח wall
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: By רב אחלי's rule, a gap under four טפחים needs nothing, so building just over three טפחים should suffice instead of four.

steps.title: A courtyard is different from an alleyway
steps.stepSummary: First answer: רב אחלי's rule about gaps under four applies to a מבוי. שמואל was speaking about a חצר, which is stricter.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you wish, say: here we are dealing with a courtyard, and there with an alleyway.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by saying the two rulings deal with different places.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אחלי's leniency, that a gap under four טפחים needs nothing, was said about a מבוי. In a חצר, even a smaller gap needs to be dealt with. So שמואל's demand for four טפחים in a courtyard stands.

keyTerms.meaning: If you wish, say: introduces one of several possible answers

phrases.english: If you wish, say:
here, in a courtyard
phrases.notes: 'Here' means שמואל's instruction.

phrases.english: there, in an alleyway
phrases.notes: 'There' means רב אחלי's rule.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: כָּאן — בְּחָצֵר, כָּאן — בְּמָבוֹי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the difficulty of Steps 28 and 29.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב אחלי's rule about gaps under four applies everywhere, so three and a bit should be enough.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב אחלי's rule applies only to a מבוי. In a חצר, שמואל requires four טפחים.

steps.title: רב אחלי's rule is itself a dispute among תנאים
steps.stepSummary: Second answer: רב אחלי's rule is not agreed on by everyone. שמואל follows the תנא who disagrees with it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you wish, say: רב אחלי's rule itself is a matter of dispute among the תנאים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second, separate answer to the same question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the גמרא does not divide between courtyard and alleyway. Instead, it says that whether a gap under four needs nothing was debated by the תנאים. שמואל holds like the opinion that does not accept that leniency.

keyTerms.meaning: It is a dispute among the תנאים

steps.whatToRemember: שמואל's demand for רוב דופן is defended in two ways. Either a חצר is stricter than a מבוי, or רב אחלי's 'up to four' rule is a disputed opinion that שמואל does not follow.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
Rav Achlei's rule itself is a dispute of Tannaim.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: דְּרַב אַחְלַי גּוּפֵיהּ תַּנָּאֵי הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: An alternative answer to the same difficulty addressed in Step 30.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב אחלי's rule is accepted by everyone.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב אחלי's rule depends on a dispute among תנאים, and שמואל follows the stricter side.

steps.title: A sea inlet entering a courtyard
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that one may not draw water on שבת from a sea inlet that enters a חצר, unless there is a partition ten טפחים high.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: a narrow inlet of the sea that enters a courtyard may not be drawn from on שבת, unless it has a partition ten handbreadths high.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא about a breach in a courtyard caused by water. This sets up the questions that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sea inlet counts as a כרמלית, so drawing water from it into the חצר is forbidden. A partition ten טפחים high at the breach makes the inlet part of the courtyard. Then drawing water is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: A 'tongue' of the sea: a narrow sea inlet

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
a tongue of sea that enters a courtyard
phrases.notes: A narrow inlet that breaks into one of the courtyard's walls.

phrases.english: one may not fill water from it on Shabbat

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן יֵשׁ לוֹ מְחִיצָה
phrases.english: unless it has a partition
ten handbreadths high.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: לְשׁוֹן יָם הַנִּכְנָס לְחָצֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Introduces a new source about a courtyard breached by water.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may not draw water on שבת from a sea inlet entering a courtyard unless there is a partition ten טפחים high.

steps.title: The partition is needed only for a breach wider than ten
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא limits its rule. A partition is needed only if the breach is wider than ten אמות. If it is ten, nothing is required.
steps.simpleTranslation: When is this said? When the breach is more than ten. But if it is ten, nothing at all is needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues and narrows when its rule applies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A gap of up to ten אמות is treated like a doorway, so the courtyard stays enclosed. Only a wider gap breaks the enclosure. Only then is a partition needed before one may draw water.

keyTerms.meaning: In what case are these words said: introduces a limitation
A breach or gap in a wall

phrases.english: In what case is this said?
where its breach is more than ten
phrases.notes: Ten אמות.

phrases.english: but if it is ten, nothing is needed.

steps.triggerLanguage: בַּמֶּה דְּבָרִים אֲמוּרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the ruling of Step 32 to breaches wider than ten.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The partition is needed only when the breach is wider than ten אמות. At ten or less, nothing is needed.

steps.title: How can one carry in a courtyard fully open to a forbidden area?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא suggests that only drawing water is forbidden, so carrying within the courtyard is allowed. But the courtyard is breached along its whole width into a forbidden area.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is only filling water that we may not do, which implies that carrying we may do. But the courtyard is breached completely into a place forbidden to it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws an inference from the ברייתא and then challenges it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the ברייתא forbids only drawing water, it implies that carrying inside the חצר is fine. But a breach wider than ten אמות opens the courtyard to a כרמלית. That should break the enclosure, so carrying within the courtyard should also be forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: A place forbidden to it: an area one may not carry into from the courtyard

phrases.english: It is filling that we may not do
which implies that carrying we may do.
But the courtyard is breached along its entirety
into a place forbidden to it!
phrases.notes: The sea inlet is a כרמלית.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִמְלָא הוּא דְּלָא מְמַלְּאִינַן, הָא טַלְטוֹלֵי מְטַלְטְלִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an inference from the ברייתא and challenges it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The implied permission to carry inside the courtyard
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A courtyard fully breached into a forbidden area should lose its enclosure, so carrying inside it should be forbidden.
